markdown:
**Source** [Pathfinder #196: The Summer That Never Was](/Sources.aspx?ID=214) pg. 22 **Complexity** Simple Beams of heavy and sharp wood rest against one another to form a precariously balanced cage tied to several trip lines and tension-bearing dowels. --- **Stealth** DC 17 (trained) to notice how the pile might fall on a person disabling it; DC 0 to see the pile. **Disable** DC 17 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) (trained), [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) (trained), or [Engineering Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) (trained) to figure out how to safely dismantle the pile without it collapsing on anyone. **Collapse Inward** **Trigger** Any of the four revelers within the hazard perform any action with the [Move](/Traits.aspx?ID=114) trait; **Effect** The pile collapses onto the four revelers, dealing 1d6+5 bludgeoning damage (DC 17 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save) to each of them. All four also take 1d6 persistent [bludgeoning damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) until they're pulled from the rubble with a DC 17 [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) check or can [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) (DC 17).
**Collapse Outward** **Trigger** An attempt to disable the hazard from outside critically fails, or the hazard is intentionally triggered by someone from outside of the wood pile; **Effect** The pile collapses outward, inflicting 1d6+5 bludgeoning damage to the four revelers (DC 15 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save), and 2d6+5 bludgeoning damage (DC 17 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save) to all creatures in a 10-foot area surrounding the central 10-foot-square where the revelers were trapped.
